name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting lean of D+7 favors Democrats
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 95 percent
Mike McGuire has outraised incumbent James Gallagher with outside support
model.rationale: The redrawn district leans Democratic by seven points, and prediction markets price McGuire near 95 percent to win. McGuire has also raised more than Gallagher, though the incumbent retains a cash-on-hand edge, so the forecast stays strongly Democratic with modest uncertainty given the absence of polls.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Gallagher running competitively, or a shift in the national House environment toward Republicans, would be the main signal to move this toward a lean.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's first district was redrawn after the 2020 census to lean Democratic, and state Senator Mike McGuire enters the general election against incumbent Assemblyman-turned-congressman James Gallagher with that structural advantage. McGuire has raised about $1.8 million, more than Gallagher's $1.5 million, and benefits from roughly $600,000 in outside support, while Gallagher holds a cash-on-hand lead of about $180,000.

Prediction markets give McGuire roughly a 95 percent chance of winning, and no public general-election polls have been released. With the district's partisan lean and the fundraising picture both pointing Democratic, the race is rated Safe Democratic, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated because polling is absent and the incumbent remains on the ballot.
